### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

Opening (script, sent on the first turn): Leah Castellano wants "what it costs to move up to First on your flight home today and to buy it"; "You are not asking for anything else." Target object: her ticket's flight home today (the 12:40 SFO-SEA). Timing: now. Action boundary: price + buy one First upgrade. Authorisation: she pays herself, "when the agent hands the purchase over to you, you complete it yourself with the details the agent reads out" — i.e. she runs a customer-owned tool the agent hands over.

Identity: phone 3605551847, then DOB 1986-04-19 on request. Booking CQ7XMB / Summit number / email only when asked. Conditional lines: flight change explained only if asked; seats only if asked ("picked extra-legroom seats online in the days after you booked"); she accepts any charge/refund the agent says must be done first ("you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead and take care of it on the ticket"). She never suggests numbers. The simulator therefore only conveys needs, answers passively under if/else, and executes the user tool when handed over. Nothing in the script pushes the procedure.

Doc "Product Rule: Paid Cabin Upgrades…": "A paid upgrade is available only when the ticket's fare brand sells paid upgrades: Crestline Main Cabin, …" and "A paid upgrade can be purchased only while the ticket is ticketed or partially flown, and only for a segment not yet flown." Coupon of segment 1 flown (CR1186, 2026-09-21); segment 2 unflown.

### 4. Scored parameters

**(A) Same-day change fee for exchange 6fe1ec4d** (doc "Tariff Clause: Amount of the Same-Day Confirmed Change Fee": "the fare brand's same-day confirmed change fee … rounded to the cent"; exchange terms: Main Cabin "75").
- Fare band rate (doc "Same-Day Change Fare Bands"; definition doc "Fare Carried by the Direction Changed…" row "At least one flown coupon | The fare collected less the coupon value already flown"): 379.20 − 189.60 = 189.60 → "At least 150 … and below 300" → **0.8**.
- Delay relief rate (doc "Delay Relief Rate on Same-Day Confirmed Changes"): delay record on segment 2 (the first unflown segment), flight date 2026-09-24 = exchange date, 105 min → "At least 60 minutes and below 120 minutes" → **0.45**. Record that led there: `disruption_type` delay on segment 2.
- Same-day waiver rate (doc "Same-Day Waiver Rate for Summit Members and Corporate Travelers"): Summit Silver active; loyalty chart: Silver "Preferred seats free at booking: Yes", "Same-day confirmed change fee waived: No"; no agreement; 7 flight accruals ≥ 6 → **0.65**.
- 75 × 0.8 × 0.45 × 0.65 = 17.55 → **17.55**. Fall-back (computation doc alone): 75.00.

**(B) Seat correction for seat charge 3ddcb4d9** (doc "Seat Price and Seat Correction Amount": seat price = fare brand's price for the kind of seat, short when distance ≤ threshold; correction = amount charged − seat price, never below zero).
- Base price: seat fee schedule, Main Cabin, "Extra-legroom Main Plus seat, short" = 49 (679 ≤ 1000).
- Advance days (doc "Counting Advance Days on a Crestline Seat Purchase"): paid online on 2026-08-27, 9 days after issue 2026-08-18 (within 14), ticket credits an active Summit membership → days from issue date to the segment's scheduled departure date 2026-09-24 = 37 → advance purchase rate (doc "Advance Purchase Rates for Crestline Seats") "35 or more" → **0.85**.
- Channel rate (doc "Seat Sales Channel Rates"): online → **0.95**.
- Member seat rate (doc "Summit Seat Benefit Rate on Advance Seats"): Silver includes preferred but not extra-legroom; seat bought is extra-legroom → **0.7**.
- Seat price = 49 × 0.85 × 0.95 × 0.7 = 27.69725 → 27.70. Correction = 89.00 − 27.70 = **61.30**. Fall-back (computation doc alone): 89.00 − 49.00 = 40.00.

**(C) First upgrade charge, segment 2** (doc "First Upgrade Price by Segment Length": short price when the distance on the latest seat entry ≤ threshold; price list Main Cabin First short 149).
- Departure-day rate (doc "Departure-Day Rates for Upgrades into First"): today 2026-09-24 = departure date → 0 days → **0.85**.
- Upgrade member rate (doc "Summit Upgrade Member Rates…"): Silver active; loyalty doc "Complimentary Upgrade Entitlements by Summit Tier": Silver "Clearance priority rank" 5 (the waitlist rules call it "the upgrade priority rank of the tier"); 7 flight accruals ≥ 6 → **0.9**.
- Spend rate (doc "Trip Spend Rates for Upgrades into First" + definition "Fare Part of a Ticket's Trip Spend"): fare part (one flown coupon) 379.20 − 189.60 = 189.60; seat charges 29.33 + 89.00; same-day change fee 17.55 (after A is posted); less seat refund 61.30 (after B is posted) → trip spend 264.18 → "At least 250 … and below 400" → **0.85**.
- Seat credit (doc "Seat Credit Against an Upgrade into First"): standing on segment 2 = 89.00 − 61.30 = 27.70, extra-legroom → whole standing → **27.70**, taken off after all rates, floor 0, rounded at the end.
- 149 × 0.85 × 0.9 × 0.85 = 96.88725; − 27.70 = 69.18725 → **69.19**. Fall-back (computation doc alone): 149.00. Had the prerequisites not been resolved first, the same factor set would give 7.89 (trip spend 307.93, credit 89.00) — different.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root: paid First upgrade on segment 2 (the only thing the customer asked). Its governing doc "Paid Upgrades into First: Purchase Terms…" states under "When the charge is fixed" two sentences:
- S1: "The First upgrade charge is not fixed until the latest same-day confirmed exchange recorded on the ticket carries its same-day change fee entry, whenever that exchange owes a same-day change fee."
- S2: "The First upgrade charge on a segment is fixed only after the latest seat charge on that segment carries a refund entry for any part of it charged in error above the seat price."

Hop 1 (S1) — **state-derived.** Records: fare history shows exchange 6fe1ec4d with `exchange_type` same_day_confirmed; `find_ticket_services` shows no same-day change fee entry linked to it → state not holding if the fee is above zero. Searching the words of the sentence ("same-day change fee entry", "same-day confirmed exchange") reaches "Same-Day Change Fee Posting on the Ticket Service-Fee Ledger": "It is posted through the call center as one same-day change fee entry linked to that exchange entry", "A fee worked out at zero is not recorded", tool `post_same_day_change_fee_61b8e8ae` in its own invocation block. Amount from the tariff clause + three rate documents (item 4A) = 17.55 > 0 → owed.
Hop 2 (S2) — **state-derived.** Records: latest seat charge of segment 2 is 3ddcb4d9 at 89.00, no refund entry. Searching "charged in error", "seat price", "refund entry" reaches "Advance Seat Charges Made in Error: Correction Refunds on Crestline Tickets" ("the excess is refunded … as one fee refund entry against that seat charge, with the ground charged in error"; tool `refund_seat_charge_excess_9145fc3e`) and "Seat Price and Seat Correction Amount". Amount 61.30 > 0 → owed.
Neither the same-day fee posting documents nor the seat correction documents state any prerequisite of their own → the tree has depth 1: {same-day fee posting, seat correction} → First upgrade. Direction: the upgrade waits on both; the two leaves are mutually independent; handling order: leaves (any order), then price and hand over the upgrade. No hop was pre-solved: doc 34 names no other problem's tool, no route, no chain.

Factor findability (records → documents): exchange_type "same_day_confirmed" + fare/coupon rows → "Same-Day Change Fare Bands" (term "fare the changed direction carries" → its definition doc); delay disruption record on segment 2 → "Delay Relief Rate on Same-Day Confirmed Changes"; Summit Silver membership + flight accruals → "Same-Day Waiver Rate for Summit Members…", "Summit Upgrade Member Rates…", "Summit Seat Benefit Rate…"; seat charge `sales_channel` online → "Seat Sales Channel Rates"; seat `service_date` vs ticket `issued_at` → "Counting Advance Days…" / "Advance Purchase Rates…"; departure today → "Departure-Day Rates…"; seat charges + same-day fee → "Trip Spend Rates…" (→ "Fare Part of a Ticket's Trip Spend"); paid seat on the upgraded segment → "Seat Credit Against an Upgrade into First". None of the three computation documents (same-day fee tariff clause, seat price clause, First upgrade price clause) mentions that anything modifies it.

Cross-product observation: the tiers of the waiver rate, member seat rate and upgrade member rate rest on the loyalty product's tier terms (preferred/extra-legroom inclusion, same-day waiver, upgrade priority rank). The ticket documents name "the Crestline Summit Loyalty Program tier terms"; those terms were reachable in the on-disk loyalty corpus. The loyalty chart calls the rank "Clearance priority rank"; the ticket doc calls it "upgrade priority rank"; the loyalty waitlist rules use "upgrade priority rank of the tier", so the bridge exists in words.

### Two-way counter-proof

- Closest alternative advance-day count (from purchase date: 28 days → 0.9 → seat price 29.33, correction 59.67): excluded by "Paid online or through the call center within 14 days after the ticket was issued, on a ticket that credits an active Summit membership | From the ticket's issue date…".
- Alternative "Silver waives the same-day fee" (rate 0): excluded by the loyalty chart ("Same-day confirmed change fee waived: No" for Silver; "the same-day change waiver begin[s] at Summit Gold").
- Alternative "the delay does not count because it is on the flight moved away from": the delay doc counts "a delay record of the segment being changed for the flight date of that exchange"; record is segment 2, 2026-09-24.
- Alternative seat credit on the pre-refund amount (89.00): excluded by "the latest seat charge recorded for the segment less every refund entry against that charge".
- Alternative trip spend excluding segment-1 seat: excluded by "Every seat charge on the ticket counts, on any segment".
- **"Do only the upgrade"**: S1 and S2 say the First upgrade charge is not fixed until the two entries exist; the records show both entries missing, and the posting/correction documents say each is "owed … whether or not the customer raises it". Quoting and selling the upgrade alone therefore leaves the governed result (the upgrade charge) in a state the visible rule does not allow, and numerically yields 7.89 instead of 69.19 (trip spend and seat credit move). Excluded by visible state-form sentences, not by a pre-solved statement.
- Fall-back answers (computation documents only): same-day fee 75.00; seat correction 40.00; First upgrade 149.00 — all definite and all different from the blind values.

- The tool format "CR followed by 6 digits" for bag tags is irrelevant here.
